head.title: Human Technology in Sports and Medicine

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Mathematics & Physics, Biomechanics and Mechanobiology, Data Management and Data Analysis, Anthropometry and Ergonomics/Sports Science, Sports Sciences, Material & Construction, Orthopaedic Aids, Prosthetics, Orthotics, Bionics, Robotics/Orthopaedic Technologies, Footwear and Floors/Footwear, Apparel and Playing Surfaces, Sports Equipment and Sportswear/Sports Equipment and Instrumentation, Modelling and Simulation, Materials Testing and Performance Diagnostics/Performance Diagnostics in Sport, Medicine and Rehabilitation

data.headline: Target group
data.text: The study programme M.Sc. Human Technology in Sports and Medicine addresses students with a passion for science and a wide interest in the interaction between humans and technology. The Master's course in Human Technology in Sport and Medicine fills the niche between engineering sciences and sports and medical science. The aim of this course is to build a bridge between sports equipment, machines and clothing as well as technological orthopaedic aids. The degree programme is aimed at people who have a strong affinity with the subjects of science and engineering and also possess a basic understanding of human movement and the human body. Furthermore, they should also be curious and creative, enjoy developing ideas and creating and reviewing new concepts.

items.name: Deadlines
text: Please enquire

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Sufficient command of the English language is to be proven by applicants. The following proofs are accepted: TOEFL (IBT) (at least 90 points), IELTS (at least 5.5), Cambridge Test CAE, FCE (at least grade B) or certificates certifying language proficiency at level B2 GeR (e.g. higher education entrance certificate).

During the course an internship of at least 6 weeks at a time is planned.

Students are advised to commence studies in the winter semester.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
1) Bachelor of Science with a grade of at least 2.5 in Business Informatics or related / comparable degree programs, or in Business Administration with a specialisation in Business Informatics or Computer Science, or in the Computer Science degree program.

2) Applicants with a Bachelor's degree from another field of study should already have previous knowledge of Design and Implementation (programming, in particular object-oriented programming) of software systems. The scope of the achievements for the two areas in the Bachelor's degree course should total at least 30 ECTS credits. The distribution of the credits between the courses is not relevant. Also in this case, the grade of the underlying Bachelor's degree must be 2.5 or better.

3) Alternatively, a qualification equivalent to the Bachelor's degree can serve as admission requirement. Equivalence is decided by the Study and Examination Board.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Computational Neuroscience, Neurobiology, Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Neuroinformatics, Artificial Intelligence, Neurophysics

data.headline: Target group
data.text:
Area of Study and Research
The latest offshoot, the Graduate School of Neural Information Processing, started teaching in the winter term of 2011. This school covers theoretical and computational aspects of neuroscience, a field of research that has become increasingly important in the past years.

Apart from the Centre for Integrative Neuroscience CIN, major partners of this graduate school are the Tübingen Bernstein Centre for Computational Neuroscience BCCN and the newly established MPI for Intelligent Systems, which provide in addition to financial support scientists who make a considerable contribution to teaching and laboratory training.

Teaching Program Curricular Focus

- neural data analysis and models of neural coding and computation,
- computational motor control and computational vision,
- rehabilitation robotics and brain-computer interfaces,
- physical and physiological basis of neural recordings and brain imaging,
- systems neuroscience and neurophysiology,
- basic mechanisms of learning and memory,
- mathematics, statistics and programming,
- machine learning for neuroscience,
- theoretical neuroscience,
- behaviour and cognition.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Analysis of Geographical Processes and Spatial Data, Geosimulation, Geographical Process Modelling and Visualisation, Visual Geodata Mining

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates of a Bachelor's degree in Geoinformatics, Geography (with at least 20 ECTS in Geoinformatics), Computer Science with minor / application subject Geography (at least 12 ECTS) or subject-related courses at a German university

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Accredited degree programme
Approval-free without NC with selection procedure

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
1. Academic degree of a Bachelor’s course in Geoinformatics or Geography with Geoinformatics (at least 20 ECTS) or Computer Science with Geography as a minor/application subject (at least 12 ECTS) or subject-related courses at a German university.

2. Overall grade of at least 2.99 according to the General Examination Regulations of the University of Augsburg or another equivalent German or foreign academic degree in natural sciences with an equivalent overall grade.

3. Basic knowledge in a programming or script language as well as a minimum Level C1 English.

4. Subject-specific proof: at a minimum, you must have taken a lecture on geoinformatics, a lecture on cartography, a tutorial on geoinformation systems, an application course involving GIS or programming, and a programming course (language irrelevant).
Knowledge of GIS is mandatory.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:

- Applicants who have not obtained their certificate of academic degree in a signatory state of the Lisbon Convention must also demonstrate their suitability for the Master’s degree programme in Business Information Systems by completing the "Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT)" with a score of at least 600 points (10th Edition) or 565 points (Focus Edition).

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Social Sciences, Econometrics, Big Data, Data Analysis

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates with an above-average Bachelor's degree in economics/political economics, mathematics, statistics, political science, computer science, sociology or psychology.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: In our international course, you will learn how to recognise structures in large amounts of data, to extract and analyse relevant information and to draw the right conclusions from it. You can start your doctorate already during the Master's programme via the fast track option.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
You will need an above-average Bachelor's degree in business administration/economics, mathematics, statistics, political science, computer science, sociology or psychology, proof of credits in three of our Foundation of Data Analysis courses, English language skills (demonstrated by a language test such as Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English, IELTS or TOEFL), a CV with a letter of motivation and two letters of recommendation from university professors.
We will gladly receive your application even if you have not yet obtained your Bachelor's certificate. Please see our website for all the admission requirements.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Big Data, Data Analysis, Data Acquisition, Data Management, Machine Learning, Internet of Things, Statistical Modelling, Visual Analytics

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
The graduate program in Data Engineering offers a fascinating and profound insight into the methods and technologies of this rapidly growing area.

The program combines big data aspects of "Data Analytics" as well as of "Data Science" with the technological challenges of data acquisition, curation, and management.

Thus, the program provides the essentials for paving the way to a successful career: computer skills and mathematical understanding paired with practical experience in selected application fields. The Data Engineering program attracts students with diverse career goals, backgrounds, and prior work experience.

Therefore, the program offers four focus tracks within which the students can choose to specialize further: Computer Science, Geo-Informatics, Bio-Informatics, and Business & Supply Chain Engineering. These tracks are a preparation for the Advanced Projects within the Discovery Area and the Master Thesis.

Tuition for the MSc Computer Science and Software Engineering, MSc Data Engineering, the MSc Supply Chain Management and the MSc Data Science for Society and Business is EUR 20,000 per academic year.

Merit-based scholarships and financial aid packages are available.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
General information:
The application- and project-related studies in the Master's degree programme in "Business Informatics" lead to a specialisation in "practical computer science", "business informatics" and "business administration"
Courses in the field of Business Informatics are primarily offered by teachers from the practice. This leads to a high degree of practical relevance in the course of study with a study-integrated two-semester project work.

Research focuses:
The Master's degree programme expands and deepens the competences in the fields of "business "informatics", "computer science" and "business administration" You can adjust the weighting of these areas to your individual interests.

In addition to various in-depth modules from the fields of computer science and business informatics, e.g. on "cloud computing"" IT security or process "modelling, "there is also a wide selection of business administration modules from the three main areas of Accounting and Finance, Market-oriented Corporate Management or Innovation and Information". In addition, there is the possibility of choosing practice-related modules, especially in the field of business informatics.

The project-oriented study programme in the Master's degree programme Data Science consists of specialisations in computer science, e.g. in the fields of data mining, algorithms or data management, and in the mathematical area of the programme from one of the main focuses Analytics or Scientific Computing.

The aim is in particular to intensify independent scientific work.

In addition to various in-depth modules from areas of computer science, e.g. in machine learning, software development of scalable systems and big-data technology, which can be combined according to individual interests, you will choose a mathematical focus in the area of statistical data analysis (Analytics) or scientific computing.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Candidates should have a recognised first degree (Bachelor of Science or Engineering) in computer science, computer engineering, informatics or in another closely related discipline, awarded by an internationally recognised university or equivalent degree-awarding institution.

Applicants should also have a record of above-average performance during their undergraduate studies. Further, we strongly advise candidates to take the Graduate Record Examination (GRE).

Candidates are required to be able to speak and write fluent English (TOEFL 550 paper-based/213 computer-based/80 Internet-based or IELTS 6.0). English-speaking students will attend a basic German language course starting in August, 2 months prior to the beginning of the Master's programme.

modules.name: DAAD Hochschulkompass

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Analysis and optimisation of complex business processes, Assessment of Decision Alternatives, Supply Chain Management, Operations, Logistics, Capital Markets, Financial and Risk Management

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Students in the degree programme "Operations Research & Business Analytics" learn scientific methods for the analysis and optimisation of complex business processes, and for the critical assessment of decision alternatives. They are taught in-depth problem knowledge from the corresponding fields of application (supply chain management, operations, logistics, capital markets, financial and risk management), so that as graduates of the programme, they will be able to make a significant contribution to the development of solution approaches for strategic, tactical and operational problems of a company.

In particular, students are enabled to prepare and analyse large amounts of data using scientific methods and to use the data to calculate forecasts or to create decision-supporting models. In addition to providing input data for business planning models, students also learn to create mathematical models themselves, apply algorithms to calculate solutions and, if necessary, develop new methods. Thus, the analytical skills of the students are further developed and the practical solution skills are further expanded.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
First academic degree (Bachelor’s, Diploma degree, etc.) in a relevant degree course with at least 140 ECTS (at the time of application) and an average grade of at least 2.9 determined from the graded courses.

- A degree course is deemed relevant if:
A. at least 45 ECTS (EU degrees) or 9 modules (non-EU) in Economics and at least 20 ECTS (EU degrees) or 4 modules (non-EU) have been earned in courses in the field of Quantitative Methods, or
B. at least 65 (EU degrees) or 13 modules (non-EU) can be demonstrated in courses in the field of Mathematics and Statistics, Econometrics, Operations Research.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Modelling, Simulation and Validation, Visualisation and Data Science, https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/civil-engineering/studies/master-degree-programmes/digital-engineering/curriculum/

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Bachelor graduates Civil Engineering or Applied Computer Science with an interest in Industry 4.0

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: The use of digitally networked systems is progressing in all industrial sectors. The developments currently being observed under the buzzword Industry 4.0 are essentially based on the continuous digital mapping of all steps in the value chain of industrial production. From the planning phase to design/design and the production process to lifetime monitoring of products (e.g. also buildings), virtual product and process models are networked with each other to accelerate development processes, increase the quality of products and optimize production processes. These developments therefore require well-trained specialists who work at the interface between computer science and engineering. Thanks to the degree programme jointly created by Civil Engineering and Media Informatics at the Bauhaus-Universität Weimar, you will be trained flexibly and across disciplines for the challenges in the professional world of tomorrow. In the Master's degree programme in Digital Engineering, we place great emphasis on introducing you to current research questions at an early stage through projects that are defined and supervised in collaboration with industry partners, among others. The Digital Bauhaus Lab, as the university's state-of-the-art research institution, offers the best conditions for this.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: a) Cognition: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, b) Cognition: (Computational) Neuroscience, c) Cognition: Psychology, Language and Communication, d) Cognition: Mind, Ethics and Society

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates of the Bachelor's degree in Cognitive Science or closely related courses of study such as Artificial Intelligence, Biology, Computer Science, (Computer) Linguistics, Mathematics, Neurosciences, Medicine, Philosophy, Psychology or a degree course with a high proportion of computer science content, if necessary with additional conditions depending on their subject aptitude.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Cognitive science examines phenomena such as perception and attention, memory and learning, planning, decision-making and problem solving, feeling, thinking, speaking and acting. In the 1970s, it evolved from a series of scientific/technical and humanities-related individual subjects into an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary subject. On the one hand, it is about understanding cognitive phenomena in biological systems. On the other hand, the knowledge that is gained is used to create artificial systems with comparable capabilities. While cognition was originally understood as a symbol processing process in the brain, cognitive research is now interested in a broad spectrum of phenomena that often also include the body and parts of the environment. Nevertheless, methods such as those of machine learning in artificial neural networks remain central to cognitive research. However, it also uses modern measurement methods (e.g. EEG, eye tracking) and allows subjects to explore virtual realities or examines the social behaviour of primates to learn more about cognition beyond the classic laboratory situation. Philosophical questions such as those on the ethics of artificial intelligence are not neglected either.

The Master's degree programme in "Cognitive Science" gives students the opportunity to specialise at greater depth in at least two sub-fields of cognitive science – (computer) linguistics, cognitive (neuro) psychology, artificial intelligence, neuroinformatics, neurosciences and philosophy – and to develop their individual academic profile in accordance with their interests and academic background. In interdisciplinary courses, students learn to understand and establish connections between the sub-areas of cognitive science. As part of a two-semester study project, they deal intensively with a research question and develop a solution approach, present and document it and gain valuable experience in independent project management under conditions that are common in professional scientific research at universities and in industry. The master's thesis, in which students can demonstrate their research competences in detail, takes place at the end of the course.

Students of the Master's degree programme in "Cognitive Science" in Osnabrück can apply for an international double degree programme in collaboration with the University of Trento/Rovereto (Italy).

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: Qualified Bachelor's degree in a 'Cognitive Science' course or a comparable degree. Graduates from participatory or related disciplines may also be admitted. Additionally, proof of a command of English at language level B2 according to the CEFR, as well as a written application providing evidence of aptitude and motivation for the course.

data.headline: Target group
data.text:
The international Master’s program in machine learning offers a wide choice of courses in computer science and, apart from a few mandatory courses, allows students to choose their subjects according to interest. Students will attend lectures, seminars, and project lab courses under the supervision of scientists who introduce them to basic and applied research and current topics in machine learning.

To pick up on scientific trends and make the best use of the current state of research, the curriculum relies heavily on the strong research presence on site, in machine learning as well as the wider field of computer science: top-level researchers in all major methodological branches of machine learning are present in Tübingen – personnel that will actively engage in teaching for the Master’s Program Machine Learning. Since the field is obviously very young and currently developing extremely rapidly, training will naturally be based on the most recent insights and the most pressing research questions of these teaching researchers. Project work and the Master’s thesis will offer students the opportunity to develop code for research purposes and their own scientific projects.

As interdisciplinarity is an important aspect, the Master’s thesis can be supervised by a professor any sub field of computer science.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Artificial Intelligence, Neuroscience, Computational Linguistics, Neuroinformatics

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates of a Bachelor's degree course in a suitable subject, e.g. (Business) Informatics, Artificial Intelligence, Cognitive Science, (Computer) Linguistics, Mathematics, Natural Sciences, Engineering Sciences or a degree course with a high proportion of computer science, possibly with additional requirements.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
At present, economy and society are undergoing a fundamental transformation through new computer science technologies. The focus of this transformation is on keywords such as "digitisation", "Industry 4.0", "Internet of Things", "robotics", "machine learning" and "artificial intelligence". This transformation is enabling a variety of new applications and value chains. Today, for instance, complex machines can run for longer and more reliably with predictive maintenance and e-learning systems at school, university or in life-long learning are simplifying access to knowledge. Smart farming is enabling ecologically responsible yield increases in the agricultural sector and intelligent and networked assistance systems can support us in road traffic and in the health sector. In industry, intelligent systems are supporting production and the related logistics, and in the financial sector, huge amounts of data and intelligent algorithms are being used to identify connections and be able to react faster. Studying "Cognitive Computing" means contributing to these crucial future technologies: the degree course bridges the gap between the disciplines of computer science, machine learning and artificial intelligence.
The degree course in "Cognitive Computing" deals with the modelling of cognitive human abilities and their implementation in technology and achieves this through the close interlinking of the disciplines of Artificial Intelligence, Neuroinformatics, Cognitive Modelling, Computer Vision, Computer Linguistics and Neurobiopsychology. Through education and training at this unique interface between relevant disciplines, the career-integrated Master's degree in "Cognitive Computing" enables graduates to apply their acquired skills to the development of innovative, intelligent systems and services.
The aim of the degree course is the theoretical and practical teaching of the scientific fundamentals of cognitive computing and cognitive technologies so that graduates are able to implement them in concrete, economically relevant and industry-oriented applications. The career-integrated degree course is divided into a compulsory elective area which, depending on the interests of the student, offers the necessary fundamentals of machine learning, artificial intelligence, neuroinformatics, natural language processing, computer vision and neuroscience of cognition, a compulsory area consisting of an integrative interdisciplinary area, which combines methods of the respective disciplines, and a one-year study project, as well as a profile-building elective area which serves as further specialisation. The practical relevance of the degree course is ensured by close cooperation with regional and national companies, in particular as part of the one-year study project and the Master's thesis.
Graduates of the career-integrated Master's degree course in "Cognitive Computing" qualify on a broad basis for future high-tech activities in the field of digitisation, machine learning and artificial intelligence. Especially for people who want to actively shape the digital transformation in their company, this programme is a tailor-made qualification in the sense of life-long learning and continuous further education.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: The prerequisite for access to the career integrated Master's program is that the applicant has successfully completed a suitable Bachelor's degree program at a university.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
A professionally qualifying German degree or equivalent degree from a university abroad worth 180 credit points (CP) in Computer Science or another subject with study components in Mathematics modules worth at least 20 CP and Computer Science modules worth at least 10 CP. With regard to the Mathematics modules required under sentence 1, at least 5 CP must be demonstrated in the areas of Linear Algebra or Analysis and at least 5 CP in the areas of Probability Theory or Statistics. With regard to the Computer Science modules required under sentence 1, at least 5 CP must be demonstrated in the area of Algorithms and at least 5 CP in a module in which knowledge of a higher programming language, e.g. C/C++, Java or Python, has been acquired;
English language skills of level C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR)

head.title: Mannheim Master of Applied Data Science & Measurement
head.subline: part time degree programmes for professionals, distance studies, international course, part time

data.headline: Admission semester
data.text: Admission only in the summer quarter

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Research Questions, Data Generating Process, Data Curation/Storage, Data Analysis, Data Output/Access

data.headline: Target group
data.text: The Mannheim Master of Applied Data Science & Measurement enables specialists to acquire additional qualifications in the field of data collection and data analysis. Possible job profiles after graduation include Survey Methodologist, (Quantitative) User Experience Researcher (UXR), Research Scientist, (Survey) Sampling Statistician, Decision Scientist.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
The Mannheim Master of Applied Data Science & Measurement is a part-time online Master's degree. Students can take this degree anywhere in the world. The curriculum is multidisciplinary, the courses are taught by international lecturers from leading universities, statistical offices and companies worldwide.

Students can choose between three tracks and focus on the content: Survey Methodology Track, Survey Statistics Track, Data Insights Track.

Information events for prospective students take place regularly as online info sessions. The current dates can be found on the course website.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: To be admitted to the Mannheim Master of Applied Data Science & Measurement, candidates need a first academic degree (at least Bachelor), proven knowledge in mathematical or applied statistics and work experience in data generation, statistical data collection or data analysis. Candidates also need a letter of support from their employer for this career-integrated degree course. In addition, fluent English is an admission requirement (TOEFL of at least 95), because the course language is English. After the application documents have been submitted on time, an online selection interview will take place.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Digital Entrepreneurship, Digitalisation, Digital Democracy, Data Science, Digital Economics, Digital Law and Ethics, Technical Sociology, Management Theories of Digitisation

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates with a Bachelor's degree and interested in questions related to Digital Transformation and an idea for their own entrepreneurial project. The course offers professional perspectives in science, civil society, politics and business.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Meeting the challenges of the digital world and helping to shape change: In the Digital Entrepreneurship (MA) degree course, you will gain an understanding of the challenges and perspectives of a digital society. From developing and reflecting on your very own entrepreneurial solutions to major issues relating to the digital transformation in Europe, you will acquire the expertise you need to organise, plan and manage a company. Benefit from close cooperation between students and teaching staff, a modern coworking space, a network of experts from politics and business, and extensive support in planning and implementing your own project ideas.

Digital Entrepreneurship (MA) is a transdisciplinary, international double-degree programme of the European University Viadrina Frankfurt (Oder) and the Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań. You have the option of completing your Master's degree at both Viadrina and Adam Mickiewicz University. The programme is taught in English.

items: Partner institution: Adam-Mickiewicz-Universität in Republic of Poland (International degree: Master of Arts | M.A.)

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:

Knowledge of English at least at level C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference (GER / CEFR);
Study and examination achievements totalling 10 ECTS each in two of the main disciplines of the MoDE (Economics, Social Sciences, Law, Technical Sciences / Computer Science, Interdisciplinary Digitisation Research or related subjects)

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Computer-aided Logistics, Transport Policy, Regional and Environmental Economics, Statistics, Data Analysis / Data Science in Traffic Systems

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: Admission requirements to the course is a first professionally qualifying degree recognised in Germany or a degree from a state or state-recognised university of cooperative education in the field of transport or economics or from the MINT area (mathematics, information technology, natural sciences and technology) or a degree in another degree course with a strong quantitative orientation in terms of content. In addition, special knowledge in the fields of economics, business administration and quantitative methods (mathematics, statistics, econometrics, operations research, programming, data analytics) is required. Additional, English language skills at level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages are required. The proof of the special knowledge according to sentence 2 as well as the English knowledge is carried out according to the aptitude test procedure regulations for the Master's degree Transportation Economics.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Cyber-Security, IT Security, Secure Computer Systems, Privacy – Personal Data Protection in the Digital World, Cryptography, Malware, Cyber Attacks, Usable Security, Web Security, Machine Learning in Cybersecurity

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Students from all countries with a Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity or Computer Science or a Master's degree in Computer Science

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Admission requirements are:

Bachelor's academic degree from a German university or an equivalent degree course from a foreign university in computer science or a related subject (does not have to be a Bachelor's degree in cybersecurity)
English language proficiency at advanced level (usually C1)
Proof of skills that correspond to those taught in the Bachelor's degree programme in "Cybersecurity" at Saarland University in the core area of computer science, in particular in the following areas: 1. Mathematics (discrete mathematics, linear algebra, stochastics, statistics), 2. Theoretical Computer Science (Complexity Theory, Calculability), 3. Practical computer science (functional and object-orientated programming, data structures and algorithms, system architecture)
One dossier and two qualifying reports to document your interest in the study programme

data.headline: Target group
data.text:
Der interdisziplinäre Masterstudiengang Medizinische Informatik (Medical Information Sciences) bietet eine vertiefte Ausbildung, die fortgeschrittene Kenntnisse der Informatik mit spezialisierten Kompetenzen aus den Bereichen Medizin, Biologie und Gesundheitswesen kombiniert.

Die Studierenden haben die Möglichkeit, ihr Wissen durch eine breite Auswahl an spezialisierten Vertiefungsveranstaltungen weiter zu entwickeln und es in verschiedenen fortgeschrittenen Bereichen der Medizinischen Informatik anzuwenden, wie z.B. der (bio-)medizinischen Datenanalyse, der medizinischen Bildverarbeitung oder der Softwareentwicklung und Informationsverarbeitung im Gesundheitswesen.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
- Mathematik (z. B. Analysis, Lineare Algebra, Stochastik, Statistik) Module im Umfang von mindestens 15 Leistungspunkten
- Informatik (z. B. Programmierung, Datenbanken, Algorithmen und Datenstrukturen) Module im Umfang mit mindestens 25 Leistungspunkten
- Medizinische Grundlagen (z. B. Humanbiologie, Physiologie, Pathologie, Terminologie) oder in Medizinische Informatik (z.B. Medizinische Informationssysteme, Medizinische Bild- und Signalverarbeitung, Bioinformatik, Medizintechnik) Module im Umfang von mindestens 25 Leistungspunkten
- Selbstständige Projektarbeit oder Abschlussarbeit im Themenfeld Medizinische Informatik, Bioinformatik, Medizintechnik, Life Sciences, Informatik oder einem vergleichbaren Themenfeld (Modul im Umfang von mindestens 10 Leistungspunkten)
- Bachelorzeugnis oder gleichwertiger Studienabschluss mit der Gesamtnote 2,70 oder besser
- Nachweis von Englischkenntnissen mindestens auf dem Niveau B2 GER

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Course Objective

After successful completion of the degree course, you will have access to a portfolio of knowledge, skills and competencies in the field of numerical simulation, modelling of engineering problems and a profound understanding of mechanical problems. Graduates are specialised in the simulation of structures, fluids, thermomechanical processes and electromechanical interactions and are able to translate complex physical systems into mechanical models and use suitable tools to predict system behaviour by means of sophisticated numerical analyses.


Professional fields later on

The methods in the field of Computational Methods in Engineering are the future-oriented techniques that modern engineers need. Typical applications include for instance:

3D structural analyses, non-linear dynamics, optimisations, multi-body dynamics, crash simulations and acoustics in automotive engineering and general mechanical engineering
Fluid-structure interaction, structure optimisation, supersonic flight characteristics and high-temperature stresses in aerodynamics and process engineering
Material models (e.g. bones, tissue), prostheses, implants and artificial blood vessels in biomechanics and medical technology

Graduates will work professionally at the interfaces between mechanical engineering, process engineering, electrical engineering, computer science and mathematics as specialists for numerical analyses and simulations of complex technical problems. They will span the gap between the classic engineering disciplines, mathematics, computer science and software development.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Relevant Bachelor’s academic degree (at least 180 CP) and an average grade of at least 2.5 determined from the examination results

Proof of subject-related skills through
- At least 15 CP in Mathematics and Computer Science,
- 40 credit points in Engineering Principles
(including 10 credit points in Technical Mechanics, 5 credit points in Fluid Mechanics or Thermodynamics)

Application is possible if the academic degree has not yet been completed at the time of application and no more than 25 CP are missing until the Bachelor's degree programme has been successfully completed in full. This has no bearing on the proof of subject-related competencies and the determined grade point average of 2.5 at the time of application.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
The Master of Science in Computer Science and Software Engineering at Constructor University Bremen is a research-oriented consecutive master programme that complements a broad spectrum of research-oriented technological education with essential management and leadership skills to educate the future technology leaders in research and industry. To prepare students for this role of technology leaders in research and industry, it offers a solid training in Software Engineering regarding development and management, as well as technical core courses in three subject areas that are presently at the utmost importance: Software Engineering, Cybersecurity, and Artificial Intelligence.

These offers mirror the Constructor University's research-centric approach. Thereby, excellent teaching competence is guaranteed and hands-on experiences from the forefront of the state-of-the-art in research and industry are provided.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology or another discipline with at least 60 ECTS in Computer Science-related topics (such as Mathematics, Programming, Design, Software Architecture).

Tuition for the MSc Computer Science and Software Engineering, MSc Data Engineering, the MSc Supply Chain Management and the MSc Data Science for Society and Business is EUR 20,000 per academic year.

Merit-based scholarships and financial aid packages are available.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
- Excellent knowledge of Computer Sciences: Introduction to Computer Science, Programming, Algorithms and Data Structures, as well as one of the following subjects: Theoretical Computer Science, Computer Architecture, Computer Networks, or Software Engineering (minimum of 24 ECTS credits or equivalent).
- Mathematical references in analysis and linear algebra (at least 18 ECTS or equivalent).
- Necessary programming competencies in algorithms and data structures: basic data structures (arrays, lists, stacks, queues, sets, trees and graphs); Complexity analysis (best case, worst case, average case, Big-O notation, divide and conquer); Sorting algorithms (bubble sort, insertion sort, quicksort, mergesort and heapsort); Searching algorithms (linear search, binary search, tree search and graph search); Hashing techniques (open hashing and closed hashing)

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: The challenges posed to our society by new digital technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), social media and big data call for solutions that combine technological and philosophical expertise. Our Master's degree programme in Philosophy & Computer Science (P&CS) at the University of Bayreuth (subject to the approval of the Bavarian State Ministry of Science and the Arts) aims at training a new generation of scientists and creative thinkers with all the necessary skills to navigate the social, epistemological, ethical and institutional challenges of increasingly pervasive modern information technologies.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
The Master's degree programme in 'Engineering of Hydro-environmental Extremes' at the University of Siegen confers an academic degree which qualifies the title holder as a scientific and engineering consultant in the field of hydro-environmental extremes.

The course prepares graduates towards working independently within doctoral programmes in one of the related sub-disciplines of civil engineering, environmental sciences, geosciences, mechanical engineering or computer science. It also trains engineers and project managers for leading positions in industry, business and public administration.

The course is offered by the following departments at the University of Siegen:
Department of Civil Engineering
Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Department of Mechanical Engineering
Department of Architecture

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: A Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Civil Engineering dual degree, Mechanical Engineering or Computer Science at the University of Siegen, or a degree course of at least three years with a Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Environmental Sciences, Geology including Engineering and Hydrogeology, Geosciences, Geography or Geophysics at a state or state-recognised university.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Algorithms and Data Engineering, Machine Learning, Mathematical Methods, Process Mining, Deep Learning, Computer Vision, Quantum Algorithms, Natural Language Understanding, Mathematical Modelling; Statistics, High-Dimensional Probability; Ethics and Computer Science

data.headline: Target group
data.text: The degree course is aimed at students with a BSc degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics or related fields.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Admission is based on an aptitude procedure, which is laid down in Section 4 and Annex I of the examination regulations. This requires, among other things, an average grade of 2.70 or better in the previous BSc degree programme.
Furthermore, proof of the following knowledge from the Bachelor’s degree is expected:
- Multidimensional Analysis (at least 5 CP ECTS)
- Abstract Structures of (Linear) Algebra (at least 5 CP ECTS)
- Basics of an Advanced Programming Language (at least 4 CP ECTS)
- Practical Programming (at least 4 CP ECTS)
- Algorithms or Numerical Procedures (at least 5 CP ECTS)
- Discrete Structures, Databases or Data Engineering (at least 5 CP ECTS)
-Data Science or Machine Learning (at least 4 CP ECTS)

data.headline: Target group
data.text: The programme is aimed at German and international prospective students with an academic degree in a ST(E)M subject who are striving for a compact reorientation or deepening of their expertise in the field of computer science.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: Continuing education one-year Master’s degree programme with a high level of practical relevance for students who wish to take a new professional direction or specialise in the field of computer science.  The degree course is taught entirely in English. Students can study our Data Science profile or develop an individual focus.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text: Completion of a Bachelor’s degree in STEM of at least 4 years (240 ECTS), alternatively a Master’s degree in STEM or a 3-year Bachelor’s degree in STEM (with additional credits), each with a grade of at least 2.5, prior knowledge of Computer Science and Mathematics, as well as relevant professional experience of at least one year. Command of English of at least B2 level.

items.headline: Application Deadline for Aptitude Test
items.comment:
Application for the summer semester by 15 January (for everyone). 
Applications for the winter semester by 30 April (for applicants with a visa requirement) or by 30 June (for applicants without a visa requirement).

data.headline: Target group
data.text: The Master’s degree course is aimed at German or international graduates who have completed a degree in Law or have earned their Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science/Software Engineering and want to explore the interplay between law and technology. The career-integrated programme is aimed at young professionals who need to balance their studies with their current job. It is just as attractive for international students who want to spend a year at another university and participate in further academic activities such as research or language training.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
The requirement is a qualified certificate of academic degree in a suitable Bachelor’s or Master’s degree programme. Suitable degree courses are, for example, German, European or International Law, Computer Science, Business Information Systems, Cognitive Sciences, (Computer) Linguistics, Mathematics or Engineering Sciences. Participants with international (Law) degrees (EU or non-EU) are particularly encouraged to apply. For further information, see the admission regulations.

Candidates must also demonstrate good English proficiency.

items.headline: Enrollment deadline for Germans and foreign students

data.text:
The fee is payable in two instalments at the beginning of the first and second semester. In many cases, these fees are paid by the applicant’s company.

In addition, semester contributions are payable for studying at the University of Osnabrück. Depending on how much of your "study credit" you use up (standard period of study plus tolerance semester), you may also have to pay long-term tuition fees. Detailed information can be found under "Costs of the programme".

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Software Engineering, Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, Explainable AI, Computer Architecture, Computer Networks, Data Engineering, Core Computer Science, Human-Centred Computing, Information Systems

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Bachelor’s degree graduates from Computer Science and Data Science should specialise according to their interests in core computer science topics on the one hand and in concrete areas of application in computer science on the other. The curriculum therefore includes compulsory elective subjects in which basic methods of general computer science are explored in depth. In addition, four areas of specialisation are offered: Core Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Information Systems, Human-Centred Computing).

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
Degree course-specific aptitude procedure:
Applications for admission to the Master’s degree programme and the aptitude procedure in the winter semester exclusively via the electronic application portal for the winter semester by 1 June (cut-off date) and for the summer semester by 1 December (cut-off date).

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Three-stage aptitude procedure:
1) Examination of the documents to be submitted in writing
2) An essay written in English (max. 1,500 words) on a given topic (announced by 1 April for the winter semester or 1 October for the summer semester).
3) Selection interview in English (15-30 minutes) on a given topic (announced by 1 April for the winter semester and 1 October for the summer semester)
The eligibility parameters are a) existing specialist knowledge and skills in the field of computer science and b) existing methodological and problem-solving skills.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Human-Centred AI, AI for Human Computer Interaction, Information Behaviour, Computational Human-Centred AI

data.headline: Target group
data.text: Graduates of a Bachelor’s degree course in Information Science.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: The international Master’s degree programme "Human-Centred Artificial Intelligence" prepares you to develop, implement and test solutions for human-centred AI. You will be taught specialist knowledge from various disciplines: computer science, data science, human-machine interaction and psychology.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Aptitude assessment procedure:
Curricular analysis (a maximum of 54 credit points can be achieved) of the submitted documents based on professional qualifications (learning outcomes of the Bachelor’s degree programme in Information Science) and final/provisional overall examination graduation.
If the final/provisional overall examination grade is 2.5 or better and 54 credit points have been achieved, the student is eligible for the degree course. If the final/provisional overall examination grade is 2.6 or worse and/or if fewer than 54 credit points have been achieved, the student is not eligible.

Selection interview in English (15-30 minutes) on a given topic (announced by 1 April for the winter semester and 1 October for the summer semester)
The eligibility parameters are a) existing specialist knowledge and skills in the field of computer science and b) existing methodological and problem-solving skills.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science or a related field with a minimum of three years of study and a minimum average score of 2.30.

The Bachelor's program must cover the following contents as part of the study program:
(a) at least one module on Databases and
(b) at least 60 additional ECTS CPs in Computer Science events
or
(c) at least 40 further CP according to ECTS and 20 CP according to ECTS in Applied Statistics.
The CP or modules to be verified may not be internships or exercises.

Foreign students demonstrate sufficient knowledge of the German or English language at C1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference (e.g., DSH, TestDaf, TOEFL, IELTS, CAE).
The details of degree program equivalence and proof of language proficiency can be found in the examination regulations of the course, which can be accessed electronically from the main page of the degree course.

data.headline: Target group
data.text:
Bachelor graduates whose degree must include the following skills:

- 20 credits in the field of Software Technology
- at least 20 credits in the area of Theoretical Computer Science,
- at least 15 credits in the field of Technical Informatics,
- at least 15 credits in the area of Mathematical Foundations of Computer Science and
- At least 8 HP in the area of Human-Machine Interaction.

The examination board determines compliance with requirements.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text: Whether science, business or a combination of both: completing the Master’s degree course sets you up for a successful start to your professional life as a computer scientist. We don’t just focus on teaching current trends, but also explore basic concepts and methods that will remain relevant beyond the current content.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
Degree that includes the following skills:

- at least 20 CP in the field of Software Technology
- at least 20 CP in the field of Theoretical Computer Science,
- at least 15 CP in the field of Technical Computer Science,
- at least 15 CP in the field of Mathematical Principles of Computer Science and
The degree must have been completed with an overall grade of at least 3.0 and proficiency in English must be demonstrated (see Examination Regulations).

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Stochastics and Statistics, Finance and Insurance Mathematics, Accounting and Finance, Innovation and Information, Market-Oriented Company Management, Applied Mathematics, Numerics and optimisation

data.headline: Target group
data.text:
Graduates with proof of a specific Bachelor's degree course in "Business Mathematics" or a Bachelor's degree course in a relevant subject in the field of "Mathematics" or with proof of a comparable professionally qualifying domestic or foreign certificate of academic degree.

In addition to a Bachelor's degree course in "Business Mathematics" or "Mathematics", an academic degree for teaching at grammar schools (First State Examination or Master's degree course) with the teaching subject "Mathematics "entitles the holder to admission. A Bachelor's degree in another discipline qualifies for admission if at least 90 credit points (CP) have been completed in Business Mathematics modules as part of this or another degree course.

data.headline: Annotation
data.text:
General information:
The aim of the Master's degree course in "Business Mathematics" is to specialise and broaden the specialist skills acquired in the Bachelor's degree course in "Business Mathematics "or "Mathematics". In addition to advanced courses in mathematics, economics and computer science, you will be introduced to independent scientific work in the Master's degree. You will study current research literature and work scientifically on a problem from the field of business mathematics as part of your Master's thesis.

Research focuses:
Specialisations are possible in the following areas, among others:

Applied Mathematics:

- Numerics and optimisation,
- Stochastics and Statistics,
- Finance and Insurance Mathematics.

Economics:

- Accounting and Finance.
- Innovation and Information,
- Market-Oriented Company Management,
- Economics.

data.headline: Focus
data.text: Künstliche Intelligenz / Maschinelles Lernen, Data Analytics, Audio- und Sounddesign, Sound Studies, Zukunftskompetenzen / Future Skills, Transdisziplinarität, Forschungsorientierung / Forschungsprojekte, Zukunftsthemen / Zukunftsgestaltung, international / englischsprachig, peer learning / team teaching

data.headline: Target group
data.text:
Der Master richtet sich an Absolvent*innen mit einem Bachelorabschluss in: Informatik, Data Science, Künstliche Intelligenz, Musik, Musikwissenschaft, Anthropologie (mit Fokus auf Klang), Kultur- und Sound Studies, Musiksoziologie oder verwandten Fächern.

Wichtig ist vor allem Interesse an: transdisziplinärem Arbeiten, Forschung und Analyse, gesellschaftlichen und technologischen Zukunftsfragen.

data.headline: Admission requirements
data.text:
- Bachelor-Abschluss
- Ausreichende Englischkenntnisse (mindestens B2 Niveau) Alternativ: vollständig in Englisch absolviertes Studium
- Einschlägige Studienleistungen in mindestens einem oder mehreren Bereichen aus: Sound Studies; Sound Design; Musik; : instrumentale/künstlerische Ausbildung, Musik-Wissenschaft/-Geschichte/-Vermittlung/-Pädagogik; Gender/Queer/Postcolonial/Critical Disability/Science and Technology Studies; Kulturwissenschaften, Anthropologie, Transdisziplinäre Studien; (Musik-)Soziologie: Quantitative Sozialforschung und Statistik, Qualitative Sozialforschung, Gesellschaftsanalysen; Data Analytics, KI, Mathematik, Programmierung, Computer Science – nachgewiesen durch das Transcript of Records
- Mögliche Skills in einem oder mehreren Bereiche(en) dieser Auswahl: Audio-Recording (digital oder analog); Programmierung/Softwareentwicklung; – nachgewiesen durch den Lebenslauf und/oder Zeugnisse, Zertifikate, das Transcript of Records o.ä.
